key_insight: MedDDC-Eval separates evidence-gathering quality from final diagnosis generation, making multi-turn medical agent evaluation more fair and interpretable.
clinical_relevance: This matters for patient-facing consultation systems because it better measures whether an agent asks useful questions and collects enough history before concluding.
method: Uses a shared frozen reader so different histories are judged with the same diagnosis mapping.
Evaluates open-ended responses with directional semantic coverage and one-to-one matching for precision/recall counts.
Adds a D/T/E harness to track diagnostic usefulness, information acquisition, and efficiency during multi-turn consultations.
evidence_signal: Across two held-out sources, changing only the diagnostic reader shifted diagnosis F1 by 2.2-19.0 points and reversed 18% and 36% of policy pairwise rankings on the Record and Dialogue splits; GRPO training improved total score by 9.7 and 4.6 points on the 100-case Record and 70-case Dialogue splits.
watch_item: Results depend on the chosen frozen reader and evaluation setup, so real-world deployment should still validate whether the measured history quality matches clinical usefulness.
paper_title: MedDDC-Eval: Diagnosis-Decoupled Evaluation of Multi-Turn Medical Consultation Agents
